# Gleap — Style Reference

> Greige paper desk beneath a pane of molten orange-and-lilac glass. Regular-weight Switzer on #f6f6f3, hairlines in #e7e7e4, jet pills for action, and all color poured into liquid gradient windows the interface itself cannot touch.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Gleap speaks a greige-paper product language. The canvas is #f6f6f3, product mockups sit on #ffffff cards, step panels use #edede8 tiles, and the secondary pill fills with #dbdbd2, so the whole surface stack spans only a few points of lightness. The interface has a chromatic budget of zero. Orchid #cc85de and an estimated orange exist only inside fluid gradient panels, and Sprout Pulse #22c55e appears only as a "connected" status dot inside mockups. Size alone carries hierarchy: Switzer runs at weight 400 on 192 elements, from 14px body copy to a 104px display, and only the 64px hero line is tracked tight at -2.88px. A system-ui stack renders the mocked product as a second, denser voice. Shape is binary: 200px pills for every action, and 16px or 20px radii for containers. Elevation comes from a 1px ring plus a low diffuse shadow rather than stacked drop shadows. The page reads as a calm editorial desk with one window of weather rather than a SaaS landing page shouting in brand color.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#f6f6f3` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Body background, nav fill and section ground beneath every block — a warm greige that makes pure white read as a lifted sheet rather than as background. |
| Quartz Card | `#ffffff` | `--color-quartz-card` | Product mockup cards, chat bubbles, the "New" badge and composer fields, with 53 background uses — the brightest value, so it is reserved for anything that represents the product itself. |
| Stone Tile | `#edede8` | `--color-stone-tile` | Step-card panels in "Live in minutes" and recessed tile grounds, with 9 uses — sits one step darker than canvas so cards recede instead of lifting. |
| Pebble Button | `#dbdbd2` | `--color-pebble-button` | Secondary "See it work" pill fill and quiet tonal chips, with 11 uses — the darkest greige, and it marks the alternative without competing. Do not use it as a card background. |
| Jet Action | `#191919` | `--color-jet-action` | Primary "Start free trial" pills, active segment tab, announcement bar and chat launcher, with 12 uses — the only solid dark fill, and it carries the entire CTA weight. |
| Iron Ink | `#060d25` | `--color-iron-ink` | Text inside product mockups, plus the base of every shadow tint, with 59 uses — a navy-black that quietly separates "product" from "page". Do not use it for marketing headlines. |
| Graphite Headline | `#292929` | `--color-graphite-headline` | H1, H2 and H3 headlines and the secondary-pill label — a softened black that keeps 104px type from turning harsh on greige. |
| Charcoal Ink | `#353535` | `--color-charcoal-ink` | Body paragraphs, nav links and footer text, with 114 uses, the most-used text color — the workhorse reading tone. |
| Slate Caption | `#65656d` | `--color-slate-caption` | Step-card descriptions, the grey second line of section headers and supporting copy, with 27 uses — carries de-emphasis through value rather than size. |
| Ash Meta | `#7a7d85` | `--color-ash-meta` | Timestamps, G2 rating line, mockup metadata and icon strokes, with 24 uses — the tertiary tier, used only for information the reader can skip. |
| Mist Border | `#e7e7e4` | `--color-mist-border` | Section hairlines, chat-bubble borders and mockup rings — warm grey line work that divides without drawing attention to itself. |
| Orchid Glow | `#cc85de` | `--color-orchid-glow` | Lilac tones inside the hero and "Gleap for SaaS" gradient panels — decorative-only pigment. Do not promote it to a button, link or icon color. |
| Sprout Pulse | `#22c55e` | `--color-sprout-pulse` | "Connected" check marks and online dots inside product mockups, with 3 uses — status signal only, rationed to fewer than five instances per page. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Switzer — the single marketing voice, from body copy to 104px display, almost always at weight 400 · `--font-switzer`

- **Substitute:** Switzer from Fontshare at 400 (free, the original), Inter at 400, Geist at 400. Switzer Regular draws a touch lighter and more open than Inter 400, so keep substitutes at 400 and do not bump them to 500 to compensate.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600
- **Sizes:** 12px, 13px, 14px, 15px, 16px, 23px, 27px, 32px, 64px, 104px
- **Line height:** 1.02 at 64px, 1.04 at 104px, 1.2 at 23px, 1.3 at 27px and 32px, 1.5 at 14px and 16px
- **Letter spacing:** -2.88px at 64px (-0.045em), -0.575px at 23px (-0.025em), 0.24px at 12px (+0.02em), 0 at every other size
- **Role:** Weight 400 at display sizes is the signature. A 104px headline set in Regular is massive and quiet, and it trusts scale to do the shouting that most SaaS sites give to 600 or 700. The steps 16, 23, 32 and 64 climb at roughly √2 (1.414), a wider interval than the conventional Perfect Fourth (1.333), so each tier separates cleanly without help from weight. Weight 500 appears on only 11 elements (buttons and tabs) and 600 on 4 (badges), so bold is functional, not expressive.

### system-ui — the product's own voice, used only inside mocked interface screens · `--font-system-ui`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 400 and 500, SF Pro Text at 400 and 500 (native on Apple), Roboto at 400 and 500. All three match system-ui's nominal weights stroke for stroke.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700, 800
- **Sizes:** 10.5px, 11px, 11.5px, 12px, 12.5px, 13px, 13.5px, 14px
- **Line height:** 1.3 to 1.57 (16px on 12px, 20px on 13px and 14px, 22px on 14px)
- **Letter spacing:** 0 at all sizes
- **Role:** This stack renders every inbox, ticket and integration panel at deliberately small, half-pixel sizes, so the mockups read as real software at reduced scale rather than as illustrations. The second family also marks a boundary: Switzer means Gleap is talking, and system-ui means the product is working. Weights up to 800 (3 uses) live here, which keeps heavy type out of the marketing layer entirely.

### ui-monospace — detected in extracted data but not described · `--font-ui-monospace`

- **Substitute:** JetBrains Mono at 500, IBM Plex Mono at 500
- **Weights:** 500
- **Sizes:** 12px
- **Line height:** 1.33
- **Letter spacing:** 0 at 12px
- **Role:** A single use at weight 500 inside a code-oriented mockup, most plausibly the "Kai Code" surface. Treat it as a micro-label for code tokens only.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Switzer | 600 | 12px | 1.67 | 0.24px | `--text-small` |
| caption | system-ui | 500 | 13px | 1.54 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Switzer | 400 | 14px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Switzer | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| subheading | Switzer | 400 | 23px | 1.2 | -0.575px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Switzer | 400 | 27px | 1.3 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Switzer | 400 | 32px | 1.3 | 0px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Switzer | 400 | 64px | 1.02 | -2.88px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Switzer | 400 | 104px | 1.04 | 0px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in Switzer weight 400, including the 104px display — size carries hierarchy, and weight stays out of it.
- Track the 64px hero line at -2.88px (-0.045em) and the 23px card titles at -0.575px — tightening appears only where letterforms would otherwise drift apart.
- Use #191919 as the one filled action color on 200px pills — the dark pill is the conversion signal, so no hue is required.
- Build depth by tone: a #edede8 tile under a #ffffff mockup with `--shadow-md` — the tile recedes and the product lifts.
- Draw every divider as a 1px #e7e7e4 hairline — warm line work matches the #f6f6f3 canvas instead of reading as cold grey.
- Confine #cc85de and the orange gradient to 20px-radius showcase panels or the full-bleed hero — color is a window, not paint.
- Render product UI in system-ui at 13px and 14px with #060d25 text — the second family keeps "the product" and "the pitch" visibly distinct.

### Don't

- Don't bold the headlines to weight 600 or 700 for "impact" — at 64px and 104px, Regular is the signature, and bolding turns quiet authority into a generic SaaS banner.
- Don't tint buttons, links or icons with #cc85de — the interface's chromatic budget of zero is non-negotiable, and one lilac link would make the gradient look like a theme instead of an event.
- Don't add a 1px outline to the #dbdbd2 secondary pill — Gleap pairs two filled tones, and a ghost button reintroduces the convention the system rejects.
- Don't put #ffffff cards straight on #f6f6f3 with a heavy 0 8px 24px shadow — the system lifts through a 1px ring plus a haze at 0.05 alpha, and heavy shadows read as a dashboard template.
- Don't round marketing cards to 12px or 24px — containers sit at 20px and 16px, actions at 200px, and in-between radii blur that binary shape vocabulary.
- Don't set mockup text in Switzer — system-ui at 14px is what makes the panels read as running software rather than as typeset illustrations.
- Don't use #22c55e for anything except connected or online status — green as a decorative accent would compete with the gradient and break the rationed signal.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #f6f6f3 (Paper Canvas)
- recessed tile: #edede8 (Stone Tile)
- product card: #ffffff (Quartz Card)
- headline text: #292929 (Graphite Headline)
- body text: #353535 (Charcoal Ink)
- secondary text: #65656d (Slate Caption)
- hairline: #e7e7e4 (Mist Border)
- primary action: #191919 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts and bars stay neutral, drawn in #191919, #65656d and #dbdbd2 on #ffffff, with #22c55e allowed only as a solid status dot or "resolved" marker and #cc85de allowed only as a 20% tint for a single highlighted series, so no chart outshouts the gradient panels.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: an anchor with display inline-flex, align-items center, gap 6px, height 48px, padding 0 22px, background #191919, color #ffffff, border none, border-radius 200px, and font-family Switzer (fallback Inter) at 16px, weight 500, line-height 1.5, letter-spacing 0. Append a 14px right-arrow icon in #ffffff and add no box-shadow. Beside it, place a secondary pill with the same height and radius, padding 0 24px, background #dbdbd2, color #292929, weight 400, separated by a 6px gap. On hover, lighten the primary fill to #292929 and leave the radius unchanged.

2. Build a hero section on a #f6f6f3 background inside a 1128px container. Use a two-column grid with a 1fr 1fr split and a 48px gap. In the left column, set an h1 in Switzer at 64px, weight 400, line-height 1.02, letter-spacing -2.88px, color #292929, across two lines. In the right column, place a paragraph in Switzer at 16px, weight 400, line-height 1.5, color #353535. Below it, add the Jet and Pebble pill pair 24px down. Under the pills, add a 13px fine-print line in #353535, then a 12px rating row in #7a7d85 with 12px gaps. Put 96px of vertical padding above and below the section.

3. Build a step card: a div with background #edede8, border-radius 20px, no border and no shadow. Fill the top 60% with a 24px square grid drawn in #e7e7e4 at 1px. Center a #ffffff inner card in the grid with border-radius 16px and box-shadow `0 0 0 1px rgb(231, 231, 228), 0 2px 12px 0 rgba(6, 13, 37, 0.05)`, containing system-ui 14px weight 400 text in #060d25 and rows with 10px radii. Below the grid, with 18px padding, add a title in Switzer at 14px, weight 400, color #353535, and a description in Switzer at 14px, line-height 1.5, color #65656d. Lay three cards in a row with a 6px gap.

4. Build a navigation bar: position sticky, top 0, height 60px, background #f6f6f3, border-bottom 1px solid #e7e7e4, with an inner 1128px container using flex and space-between. Put a logo on the left. In the center, place links "Solutions", "Product", "Pricing" and "Resources" in Switzer at 14px, weight 400, color #353535, with 24px gaps. On the right, place "Login" in the same style, then a 36px-tall pill with padding 0 18px, background #191919, color #ffffff, Switzer at 14px weight 400, border-radius 200px, and an arrow icon. Above the nav, add a #191919 announcement strip with centered #ffffff 14px copy and a "New" badge: #ffffff fill, #292929 text, Switzer 12px weight 600, letter-spacing 0.24px, padding 0 9px, height 22px, radius 200px.

## Components

### Pill Button — Jet (Primary)

**Role:** The single filled call to action

### Pill Button — Pebble (Secondary)

**Role:** The quiet alternative beside primary

Tonal, not outlined. It uses a #dbdbd2 background, #292929 text, no border, a 200px radius, 0 24px padding and a 48px height. The label is Switzer at 16px weight 400 with no shadow. Most systems pair a filled primary with a ghost or bordered secondary. Gleap fills the secondary with greige instead, so the pair reads as two values of one material rather than as filled versus empty. Place it immediately right of the primary with a 6px gap.

### Glass Pill Button — Over Gradient

**Role:** Secondary action on gradient panels

Frosted and translucent. It uses white at 62% alpha (decorative, not a system token), backdrop-filter blur(14px) saturate(1.3), #191919 text, a 200px radius, 0 22px padding and a 48px height. The label is Switzer at 16px weight 500, and the shadow is an inset `--shadow-subtle-2` ring. It is a deliberate system outlier, the only translucent surface on the page. It exists because #dbdbd2 would muddy against molten orange, so it is allowed only on top of gradient panels.

### Navigation Bar

**Role:** Sticky top bar for the site

Flat, centered, low. The bar is sticky, 60px tall and filled with #f6f6f3, with a 1px #e7e7e4 bottom hairline. The logo sits left, the "Solutions", "Product", "Pricing" and "Resources" links sit centered, and "Login" plus a compact CTA sit right, all inside the 1128px container. Links are Switzer at 14px weight 400 in #353535, with dropdown triggers at 16px. The CTA is a #191919 pill with a 200px radius, a 36px height, 0 18px padding and Switzer at 14px weight 400. The nav matches the canvas rather than floating as glass, so it reads as part of the page.

### Announcement Bar with New Badge

**Role:** Release callout above the nav

Thin inverted strip. It is a full-bleed #191919 band about 44px tall (estimated), with centered #ffffff Switzer copy at 14px weight 400 and an underlined "Learn more" link. The "New" badge leads it: #ffffff fill, #292929 text, a 200px radius, 0 9px padding, a 22px height and Switzer at 12px weight 600 with +0.24px tracking. This is the only place uppercase-adjacent micro-tracking appears, which marks it as signage rather than prose.

### Segment Tabs — Industry Switcher

**Role:** Switches the industry showcase content

Pill-shaped radio row. Each tab is 40px tall with a 200px radius, 0 16px padding and Switzer at 14px weight 500 with a 1.0 line height. The active tab fills #191919 with #ffffff text, and inactive tabs are transparent with #191919 text and no border. The selected state reuses the exact primary-CTA fill rather than introducing a highlight color, which keeps the chromatic budget at zero even for interactive state.

### Step Card — Main Content Card

**Role:** Onboarding step with mockup preview

Recessed, borderless, gridded. The card uses a #edede8 background, a 20px radius, no border and no shadow, with a faint square grid pattern behind its upper half. An inset #ffffff mockup with a 16px radius and `--shadow-md` floats in that grid area. Below, a Switzer 14px weight 400 title in #353535 sits above a Switzer 14px description in #65656d, with 18px padding. Cards sit three across with a 6px gutter. The darker tile pushes the white mockup forward, so depth comes from tone rather than from the card's own shadow.

### Product Mockup Panel

**Role:** Live product UI rendered in HTML

Real software at reduced scale. The panel is #ffffff with a 16px radius, 0 padding and `--shadow-md` (a 1px warm ring plus a 2px 12px haze). Text is system-ui at 14px weight 400 in #060d25, with meta in #7a7d85 and status in #22c55e. Inside, 10px and 12px radii shape rows and tiles, avatars use 50% and 6px radii, and filter chips use a 999px radius. These are built in HTML rather than screenshots, so they stay crisp and on-palette at any zoom.

### Composer Input — Rounded Field

**Role:** Reply box inside inbox mockup

The system outlier. The field uses a #ffffff background, a 34px height, a 23px radius, 0 7px 0 8px padding and `--shadow-sm`, an inset 1px warm ring with a 1px 2px haze. Placeholder text is system-ui at 14px in #060d25 with a "⌘K" hint. The 23px radius is neither pill nor card. It is half the field's height plus a fraction, tuned so a single-line composer feels like a pill without becoming a perfect capsule. It is allowed because it belongs to the mocked product, not the marketing shell.

### Gradient Showcase Panel

**Role:** Full-color hero and industry stage

Molten color, contained. The panel is 1040px wide with a 20px radius, filled with a fluid orange and #cc85de lilac gradient image and lifted by `--shadow-lg`. It carries a #ffffff Switzer display headline at 104px weight 400, rendered with a frosted glass treatment. The hero version runs full-bleed with no radius. This is the only place saturated color is permitted, so it works as a window cut into the paper rather than as a theme.

### Metric Row with Hairline Rules

**Role:** Results proof between rules

Editorial ledger. A Switzer 32px weight 400 #292929 heading ("Results teams report.") sits above a 1px #e7e7e4 rule spanning 1080px. Below the rule, three columns of figures carry #65656d captions at Switzer 14px, and a closing hairline ends the block. There are no cards, no icons and no fill. The proof reads like a printed table, the anti-convention to the usual tinted stat tiles.

### Chat Launcher — Floating Widget

**Role:** Persistent support entry point

Solid dark disc. The launcher is about 48px in diameter (estimated) with a 50% radius and a #191919 fill (estimated), holding a #ffffff speech-bubble glyph. It is fixed 24px from the bottom-right edge. It is Gleap's own product rendered live, and it repeats the jet CTA fill so the widget feels native to the page rather than bolted on.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in Switzer weight 400, including the 104px display — size carries hierarchy, and weight stays out of it.
- Track the 64px hero line at -2.88px (-0.045em) and the 23px card titles at -0.575px — tightening appears only where letterforms would otherwise drift apart.
- Use #191919 as the one filled action color on 200px pills — the dark pill is the conversion signal, so no hue is required.
- Build depth by tone: a #edede8 tile under a #ffffff mockup with `--shadow-md` — the tile recedes and the product lifts.
- Draw every divider as a 1px #e7e7e4 hairline — warm line work matches the #f6f6f3 canvas instead of reading as cold grey.
- Confine #cc85de and the orange gradient to 20px-radius showcase panels or the full-bleed hero — color is a window, not paint.
- Render product UI in system-ui at 13px and 14px with #060d25 text — the second family keeps "the product" and "the pitch" visibly distinct.

### Don't

- Don't bold the headlines to weight 600 or 700 for "impact" — at 64px and 104px, Regular is the signature, and bolding turns quiet authority into a generic SaaS banner.
- Don't tint buttons, links or icons with #cc85de — the interface's chromatic budget of zero is non-negotiable, and one lilac link would make the gradient look like a theme instead of an event.
- Don't add a 1px outline to the #dbdbd2 secondary pill — Gleap pairs two filled tones, and a ghost button reintroduces the convention the system rejects.
- Don't put #ffffff cards straight on #f6f6f3 with a heavy 0 8px 24px shadow — the system lifts through a 1px ring plus a haze at 0.05 alpha, and heavy shadows read as a dashboard template.
- Don't round marketing cards to 12px or 24px — containers sit at 20px and 16px, actions at 200px, and in-between radii blur that binary shape vocabulary.
- Don't set mockup text in Switzer — system-ui at 14px is what makes the panels read as running software rather than as typeset illustrations.
- Don't use #22c55e for anything except connected or online status — green as a decorative accent would compete with the gradient and break the rationed signal.

| 0 | Paper Canvas | `#f6f6f3` | Page ground, nav fill and section backgrounds |

## Elevation

- **Product mockup cards (inbox, connect-your-stack):** `0 0 0 1px rgb(231, 231, 228), 0 2px 12px 0 rgba(6, 13, 37, 0.05)`
- **Composer field and inset inputs:** `inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(230, 230, 227), 0 1px 2px 0 rgba(6, 13, 37, 0.04)`
- **Floating popovers and secondary mockup layers:** `0 1px 2px 0 rgba(6, 13, 37, 0.04), 0 6px 18px 0 rgba(6, 13, 37, 0.05)`
- **Gradient showcase panels and top-level floating elements:** `0 1px 2px 0 rgba(6, 13, 37, 0.06), 0 12px 40px -12px rgba(6, 13, 37, 0.28)`
- **Chat bubbles and small chips:** `0 1px 2px 0 rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.05)`
- **Avatar stacks:** `0 0 0 2px rgb(255, 255, 255)`
- **Pressed or selected tiles:** `inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgb(207, 207, 202)`
- **Glass pill over gradient:** `inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7)`

Every shadow is tinted with #060d25 rather than neutral black, and the alpha never exceeds 0.06 except the -12px-spread 0.28 drop on showcase panels. The rule: a ring defines the edge, and a haze implies the lift.

## Imagery

The page uses no photography. The visual content splits into two categories. The first is HTML-built product mockups — inbox lists, integration connectors, a channel picker with Widget, Email, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Slack and Telegram tiles — framed in #ffffff panels with a 16px radius and `--shadow-md`, often set on a faint square grid inside #edede8 tiles. The second is fluid, liquid-marble gradient art in orange (estimated #f07c30, decorative, not a system token) and #cc85de lilac, used full-bleed in the hero and inside 20px-radius showcase panels behind frosted glass display type. Icons are monochrome line glyphs at 1.5px stroke in #7a7d85 or #191919, and third-party brand marks keep their own colors only inside 12px-radius integration tiles. Customer logos render in solid black. The gradient is decorative only and never becomes a token. The narrative: a calm, paper-quiet tool, interrupted by bursts of molten energy that stand for the AI working underneath.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1128px container, with headlines and hairline rules running 1080px wide. Sections are separated by 96px gaps, with visible air well beyond that between major blocks. The hero opens with a full-bleed gradient panel carrying "Gleap 2" in glass type, then drops to a two-column split: the 64px headline on the left, and on the right a paragraph, the Jet and Pebble pills, a fine-print line and a G2 rating row. Below it, a logo row pairs a left-aligned caption with two to four logos. Sections alternate between canvas-only typography blocks (metric rows between hairlines) and card rows. The step cards run three columns, and showcases run as one 1040px panel. The sticky nav is 60px, filled #f6f6f3, with the logo left, links centered and Login plus CTA right. A 44px #191919 announcement bar (estimated) sits above it. The footer is a tall multi-column link index on canvas. At 375px, the hero headline drops to 32px (`--text-heading`), the 104px display drops to 64px, and section gaps tighten to 48px. Density: spacious.

## Quarantined Chroma

Gleap holds a strict separation: color is weather, and the interface is paper. Every saturated pixel, the orange and #cc85de lilac, lives inside gradient art, either full-bleed in the hero or inside 1040px panels with 20px radii. Nothing interactive carries a hue. The primary CTA, active tab and launcher are all #191919, and the only exception is #22c55e as a status dot inside mockups. This breaks the moment a designer colors a link lilac, tints the secondary pill orange or adds a brand-colored icon set, because the gradient then reads as a theme instead of an event. To extend the system, add new color only as another contained gradient panel or as a status signal inside product UI, and keep every control on the greige-to-jet value ladder.

## Regular-Weight Authority

The second discipline is typographic: Switzer at weight 400 from 14px all the way to 104px, with hierarchy built from size steps of roughly 1.414 rather than from weight. Most B2B sites set display type at 600 or 700 and lean on bold to signal importance. Gleap does the opposite and lets a 104px Regular headline feel enormous through scale and air alone. The tracking is surgical: -2.88px only at 64px, -0.575px at 23px, and 0 everywhere else. Bolding a headline, adding a 500-weight subhead tier or tracking body copy would each dilute that restraint. To extend the system, add a new tier by choosing a size on the √2 ladder, keep it at 400, and apply negative tracking only above 40px.

## Similar Brands

- **Gleap** — Like Intercom, a category competitor in AI customer service, it sells through live product mockups, but Gleap drops Intercom's brand blue for a zero-hue interface on #f6f6f3 greige.
- **Gleap** — Like Stripe, it uses a fluid mesh-gradient hero as its emotional signature, but Gleap confines the gradient to bounded panels and keeps all controls monochrome.
- **Gleap** — Like Mercury, it pairs a warm off-white canvas with regular-weight display type and dark filled pills, and it reads as a ledger rather than a dashboard.
- **Gleap** — Like Plain, a fellow support-tool brand, it builds proof from crisp HTML-rendered inbox UI in system-ui on near-white cards with hairline rings.
- **Gleap** — Like Attio, it relies on 1px rings plus low-alpha haze shadows instead of drop shadows, and it treats pill-shaped dark CTAs as the only solid fills.
